narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. Because of this, the company has decided to deny your promotion.

The decision was driven most strongly by three aspects of your profile. First, having over 11 years of total professional experience was the biggest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. While only 15% of employees predicted to stay have this much experience, the model sees long overall careers as a signal that someone is more likely to move on. Second, your relatively short time in your current role—just 1 to 5 years—also pulled the prediction toward leaving; most people the model expects to stay have been with their organization longer. Third, the fact that you have not received other job offers recently worked in the opposite direction, modestly encouraging the model to think you might stay.

Taken together, your extensive background and relatively brief tenure here outweighed the stabilizing effect of not having external offers, leading the system to conclude you are more likely to leave than to remain.

The organization should review whether your long experience is being fully utilized and consider clearer career paths that encourage retention. You may want to discuss your long-term goals with your manager to see how they align with staying and growing here.
